clue.text: Cook able to hold carrier for shopping

indicators.note: to hold means the scrambled letters wrap round the carrier
to cook the books is to falsify them, so these letters are doctored into a new order

parts.note: a tray is something you carry things on

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: a capable cook is told to keep hold of a shopping bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopping' is slang for informing on someone, not buying groceries; 'Cook' shuffles the word able before the carrier goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police, an act of treachery.

clue.text: Spring, with an extremely rainy March

indicators.note: extremely means take only the first and last letters of rainy

explanation.surface: A wet and blustery spring month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' and 'March' look like seasons; spring is a leap, and a march is a borderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is an old word for a frontier or border region.

clue.text: Last in Knesset to behave wholly in a diplomatic way?

indicators.note: last in means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone at the Knesset, Israel's parliament, is told to behave diplomatically.
explanation.walkthrough: The Knesset is Israel's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with discretion and sensitivity to avoid offence.

clue.text: Swing cat — it's a superior room

indicators.note: to swing is to sway about, so these letters are swung into a new order

explanation.surface: No room to swing a cat, but this is an upper room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swing' rearranges CAT and IT. 'Superior' means higher up in the house, not better.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft room sits at the top of the house, above all the others.

clue.text: A writer's attribute

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A characteristic belonging to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attribute' looks like a noun but is the verb; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to a source or cause is to assign it.

clue.text: Gamble on large return could keep one in suspense

indicators.note: on means the word for gamble is placed after the reversed word for large
return means the word for large is read backwards

explanation.surface: A punter's big wager on a horse keeps them on tenterhooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspense' is literal: a hanged body is suspended, so the surface's tension is a grim pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallows-like post from which executed bodies were hung, literally keeping someone suspended.

clue.text: Take responsibility for debts without interest

parts.note: to incur a cost is to take it on
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Someone accepts debts that carry no interest charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks financial, but it means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking curiosity, not wanting to know.

clue.text: Money commonly raised, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for raised is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: children or animals raised are bred

explanation.surface: Money is commonly raised, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: BRED (raised) sounds the same as the slang word for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash, as in earning a living.

clue.text: Touching offer

definitions.meaning: ... in the sense of moving or affecting the feelings
to put forward formally, as a bid or resignation

explanation.definitionFit: A moving gesture is gentle and affecting; to tender a bid is to put it forward.

clue.text: Block causing elevated motorway deep trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means the motorway letters are read upwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway

indicators.note: trouble means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An elevated motorway is causing deep trouble by blocking traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: MI (the M1) reads upwards as IM; 'trouble' rearranges DEEP into PEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct or hinder progress.

clue.text: Some pages may be so exempted from censorship

definitions.meaning: a book's pages may be left with their folded edges not slit open
a film or text released with nothing cut out

explanation.definitionFit: Untrimmed pages and an unexpurgated text are both left without any cutting done to them.

clue.text: Arrive with fresh request for admission

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with a new plea to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admission' means confessing, not entry: the phrase is what you say to urge someone to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperative urges a person to confess the truth, which is asking them for an owning-up.

clue.text: I have to go on leave for not working

indicators.note: to go on means the contracted pronoun phrase is placed after the word for leave

parts.note: to defect is to leave one's country or side

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are taking leave because they are off sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like holiday, but here it means desert one's side.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty machine is one that fails to function.

clue.text: Highland feature taken to heart by poet

indicators.note: taken to heart means only the core of the poet's name is kept, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: Robert Bridges was Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930

explanation.surface: A Scottish landscape is cherished by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the heart of BRIDGES (Robert Bridges, a British Poet Laureate) by dropping its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow raised crest of land is typical of upland country.

clue.text: Renew the tenancy — free!

definitions.meaning: to let a property again on a new agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Re-letting a property under fresh terms; also to let go or liberate.

clue.text: For No. Ten a new P.M.

indicators.note: new means these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Downing Street gets a new Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'P.M.' looks like Prime Minister (No. 10 is Downing Street, the PM's home), but means post meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: Post meridiem covers the hours after midday.

clue.text: Selfish individual, say, is conspicuous in the scriptures

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: being conspicuous in something means standing inside it in view, so the word is goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone self-centred, for instance, stands out in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: OT is the standard abbreviation for the Old Testament; 'conspicuous' is part of the indicator, saying the word sits visibly inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person absorbed in self-interest puts themselves first.

clue.text: A number perhaps sit around in firm

indicators.note: in means the reversed word goes inside the word for firm
around means the word sit is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Perhaps a crowd sits around in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun but is an adjective meaning fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A single figure in a set of data, such as a count, is an example.

clue.text: Parsimony puts girl in difficulty

indicators.note: puts the girl in means her name is placed inside the word for difficulty
puts the girl in means her name is placed inside the word for difficulty

parts.note: a mess is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Stinginess lands a young woman in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinginess, unwillingness to spend.

clue.text: Arrangements to stay on the outskirts of Surrey

indicators.note: on means the word for stay comes after the county's edge letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters only

parts.note: to stay a flow is to stem it

explanation.surface: Plans for a visit to the fringes of a county south of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London; 'stay' means check or halt, as in stemming a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised set of methods or procedures is an ordered scheme.

clue.text: A handy book

parts.note: a reference book you keep at hand, also an adjective for things done by hand

explanation.definitionFit: A handbook of instructions, and also something worked by hand.

clue.text: Develop, for example, back land

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for example is read backwards

parts.note: a land is a state or nation

explanation.surface: A planner suggests developing, say, the back land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns EG into GE, followed by STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry young in the womb, or to let an idea grow over time.

clue.text: Fellow carrying weapon in jacket, perhaps

indicators.note: carrying means the word for fellow holds the weapon inside it

explanation.surface: A man carries a gun hidden in his jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is one example of an article of clothing.

clue.text: Sticker to permit entry by one member

indicators.note: entry by means the following pieces enter the word for permit

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A badge allowing one MP into the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticker' looks like a label, but means something that clings.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish that clings tightly to rocks, so a byword for anything that clings.

clue.text: Some exotic horticulture producing a divine flower

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Exotic gardening yields a heavenly bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ethereal fluid flowed in the veins of the gods instead of blood.

clue.text: Writer of an annual, it may be said

definitions.text: of an annual, it may be said
definitions.meaning: a plant that grows and flowers in one year and survives frost is described this way

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy wrote Tess; a robust bedding plant that tolerates frost is a hardy annual.

clue.text: Managed returns to share account

indicators.note: returns means the word for managed is read backwards

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A firm's manager comes back to divide the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns RAN into NAR, followed by RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken or written telling of events is a story or report.

clue.text: On the move in a prison

explanation.surface: Something is moving inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and about, stirring into activity.

clue.text: For each drink, note, use filter

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions for every drink: write it down and strain it.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is the seventh note in the do-re-mi scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is made by letting water seep through grounds in a strainer.

clue.text: Old hat with sort of shirt lining has style

indicators.note: lining means the shirt letter sits inside the word for hat, like a lining

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned hat lined with shirt fabric is stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like 'out of date' but is TILE, old slang for a hat; T (as in T-shirt) goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a name or rank by which they are called.

clue.text: Testing hearing

definitions.meaning: a judge hearing a case in court

explanation.definitionFit: Taxing describes something exasperating; also a court examining a case is doing so.

clue.text: Decoys retreating army land divisions

indicators.note: retreating means the abbreviation for army is read backwards

explanation.surface: Decoy troops retreat across divided territory.
explanation.walkthrough: TA (Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force) reversed gives AT, followed by TRACTS. 'Decoys' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure is to draw something towards oneself.
